lines.cap: **Narrator:** This is Kavya. She is twelve. In one week, she has her Science practical test: build a circuit.
**Kavya:** I've watched four videos about circuits. I've built zero circuits. My plan is confidence.
**Narrator:** But this documentary is not about Kavya. It is about a drawer.
**Narrator:** Behind Lab Three, there's a drawer: 'Electricity and Magnetism. Do not touch.'
**Cecil:** Hi. Cecil. I'm a **cell**. **1.5 V**.
**Cecil:** And no, I'm not a battery. A **battery** is two or more cells joined together. I'm one cell.
**Cecil:** I've been in this drawer since twenty fifteen. Still a perfect **1.5 V**. I don't get out much.
**Cecil:** Last year, a boy in Year Eight used a rubber band as a wire. We don't talk about it.
**Narrator:** Drawer 8B. Episode twelve: The Practical.
**Narrator:** Monday. Practice run one: a cell, a lamp, and two wires.
**Dimitri:** At last! Dimitri. The **lamp**. The star of every circuit.
**Cecil:** Dimitri thinks the circuit exists so he can shine. Honestly? It sort of does.
**Narrator:** In the copper wire live the **electrons**: tiny particles with a **negative** charge.
**Eddie:** Hi hi! Eddie! Electron! That's Eddie. That's also Eddie. We're all Eddie. It saves time.
**Narrator:** **Electric current** is the flow of **charge** around a circuit: here, the Eddies on the move.
**Cecil:** I'm the pump. I push the charge round. I don't make the Eddies. They're in the wire already.
**Kavya:** Wire from the cell to the lamp. Done?
**Dimitri:** Nothing. I feel nothing.
**Cecil:** There's a gap. Current only flows round a **complete loop**. Any gap, and it stops **everywhere**.
**Dimitri:** LIGHT! She closed the loop! I'm SHINING!
**Eddie:** And we all come back to Cecil! The current isn't used up!
**Cecil:** What gets passed on is **energy**. From me, to Dimitri, to the room, as light.
**Narrator:** Metals, like copper, are **conductors**: they let current flow. So does carbon.
**Narrator:** Plastic is an **insulator**, like rubber, glass and wood. The coat keeps the current in, and Kavya safe.
**Cecil:** Hence, the rubber band incident.
**Narrator:** Current arrows on circuit diagrams go from **+ to −**. That's called **conventional current**.
**Eddie:** But we're negative, so we really go from **− to +**! The other way!
**Cecil:** Scientists chose the direction before anyone knew electrons existed. It stuck.
**Eddie:** Two hundred years of arrows pointing the other way. Nobody asks us.
**Cecil:** In exams, draw current arrows from **+ to −**. Just be consistent.
**Narrator:** Tuesday. Two lamps **in series**: one single loop, one after another.
**Dimitri:** Two lamps? I don't share a stage.
**Cecil:** You do now.
**Narrator:** Kavya draws it first, with **circuit symbols**. In this drawer, they're on everyone's staff pass.
**Cecil:** Mine: a **long, thin** line, the **positive** side, and a **short, thick** one.
**Dimitri:** Mine: a circle with a cross. Iconic.
**Amy:** Amy. **Ammeter**. I measure **current**, in **amps**. I stand **in the line**: in **series**.
**Amy:** **0.2 A** before the lamps. **0.2 A** after. The current is the **same everywhere** in a series loop.
**Cecil:** Amy loves a queue. She queued for this interview. Nobody else was here.
**Cecil:** That's Vic. **Voltmeter**. **Voltage**, or **potential difference**, in **volts**. He stands **across** a component: **in parallel**.
**Cecil:** Vic doesn't talk. He holds up signs.
**Narrator:** In series, the cell's **voltage** is **shared**. Two identical lamps get **half** each.
**Dimitri:** Half?! I'm DIM! Do you know what it's like to be DIM?
**Cecil:** Dimitri. It's in your name.
**Narrator:** More lamps in series? They **all** get **dimmer**.
**Kavya:** And if I unscrew one...
**Narrator:** The loop breaks. In series, if one lamp goes, they **all go out**.
**Dimitri:** In the dark: betrayal.
**Narrator:** Wednesday. **Parallel**: each lamp gets its own **branch**.
**Dimitri:** I'm BRIGHT again! Nobody touch anything!
**Narrator:** Each branch gets the **full voltage** of the cell, so the lamps stay bright, even when you add more.
**Eddie:** At the junction, we split up! Some go left, some go right!
**Amy:** **0.4 A** in each branch. **0.8 A** from the cell. The branch currents **add up** to the total.
**Narrator:** Kavya unscrews one lamp.
**Dimitri:** I'm... still on. I'm still ON!
**Narrator:** If one branch breaks, the others **keep working**. So homes are wired in **parallel**.
**Kavya:** So if my brother's lamp blows, the aircon stays on. Correct priorities.
**Narrator:** Next on the worksheet: a **resistor**. Enter Auntie Rez.
**Auntie Rez:** Rez. **Resistor**. I make it **harder** for current to flow. Somebody has to.
**Amy:** **More resistance** means a **smaller current**.
**Auntie Rez:** Measured in **ohms**. Symbol: **Ω**, omega. Like a little horseshoe. Very nice.
**Auntie Rez:** Even wires resist. A **longer** wire, **more** resistance. A **thinner** wire, **more** again.
**Cecil:** Auntie Rez limits the current, to protect other components. Still annoying.
**Auntie Rez:** My nephew is a **variable resistor**, a **rheostat**. Slide him, and the lamp dims. He works in **dimmer switches** and **volume controls**.
**Narrator:** Thursday. Magnetism. Meet the drawer's longest-married couple.
**Nora:** Hello! Nora. **North pole**.
**Stan:** Stan. **South pole**. Same **bar magnet**. Forty years.
**Narrator:** The golden rule: **like poles repel**. **Unlike poles attract**.
**Nora:** Ugh. Another north pole. Get AWAY from me.
**Stan:** But a north and a south? That's how we met.
**Kavya:** What if I cut you in half? You'd finally get some space.
**Nora:** Doesn't work, sweetie. You'd get **two smaller magnets**, each with a north **and** a south.
**Narrator:** Magnets attract **magnetic materials**: **iron, steel, nickel and cobalt**. I See No Cobwebs.
**Nora:** Not all metals, though. Copper? Aluminium? Gold? We feel nothing.
**Narrator:** A **magnetic field** is the region where magnetic materials feel a force. We draw it with **field lines**.
**Stan:** Outside the magnet, they go from **north to south**, and they **never cross**.
**Nora:** They're **closest together** at the **poles**. That's where we're **strongest**.
**Narrator:** **Iron filings** show the pattern. A **plotting compass** shows the direction.
**Narrator:** A **compass** is a tiny magnet, free to spin. It points north, because the **Earth** is a giant magnet.
**Stan:** Its field comes from molten iron in its core. Near the geographic North Pole is a magnetic **south** pole.
**Stan:** Unlike poles attract. A north always falls for a south.
**Nora:** I married one.

chapters.title: The magnet with an off switch

lines.cap: **Narrator:** Friday. The **electromagnet**.
**Sol:** Hey. Sol. **Solenoid**. A coil of wire round an iron nail. Right now? A nail in a scarf.
**Narrator:** Current in a wire makes a **magnetic field**. Coil the wire, and the loops' fields add up.
**Sol:** Current's ON! North pole! South pole! I'm a MAGNET!
**Cecil:** Switched on, Sol is unbearable. Switched off, he's a nail.
**Narrator:** That's an electromagnet's big advantage: you can switch it **on and off**.
**Sol:** And... I'm a nail again.
**Narrator:** Reverse the current, and the **poles swap** over.
**Sol:** Want me stronger? **TIC**. More **turns**. **Increase** the current. Iron **core**.
**Eddie:** More current? That's more of us!
**Cecil:** And a bigger cell won't help Nora and Stan. **Permanent magnets** don't run on cells.
**Narrator:** Sol's core is **pure iron**: a **temporary magnet**. It loses its magnetism easily.
**Stan:** We're made of **steel**. **Permanent**. We keep our magnetism for years.
**Nora:** Inside us, tiny regions called **domains** all point the same way.
**Narrator:** To **magnetise** steel, stroke it with a magnet **in one direction**, again and again. The domains line up.
**Nora:** **Heat** us or **hammer** us, and they jumble. We'd be **demagnetised**. So stop dropping us, Year Eight.
**Narrator:** Scrapyard cranes lift cars with electromagnets, and switch off to drop them. **Bells**, **loudspeakers** and **motors** use them too.
**Sol:** My cousin drops a car every day. On purpose. Living the dream.
**Narrator:** Monday. Test day. Kavya combs her hair with a plastic comb. Thirty-one times.
**Kavya:** Why is my hair standing up? Why TODAY?!
**Eddie:** That was us! Rubbing two **insulators** together moves electrons, by **friction**!
**Narrator:** This is **static electricity**: charge that builds up and **stays put**, instead of flowing.
**Narrator:** The comb **gained** electrons, so it's **negatively** charged. Her hair **lost** electrons, so it's **positive**.
**Eddie:** Only electrons move! The positive charges just sit there.
**Narrator:** **Like charges repel**. **Unlike charges attract**.
**Kavya:** So all my hairs have the same charge, and they're repelling each other.
**Nora:** Likes repel, sweetie. We've been saying.
**Narrator:** The charged comb can even pick up tiny bits of **uncharged** paper.
**Narrator:** **Earthing** removes charge: a conductor to the ground lets the electrons flow away. Fuel tankers are earthed for safety.
**Kavya:** And lightning? We get it almost every afternoon here.
**Cecil:** A giant static spark, between a cloud and the ground. Very big sky static.
**Narrator:** Ten a.m. Amy in series, Vic across the lamp. It lights.
**Kavya:** Full marks. I'd like to thank... nobody. It's a drawer.
**Dimitri:** I'd like to thank... me.

chapters.title: The drawer saves you some marks

lines.cap: **Narrator:** Before the drawer closes, the cast would like to save you some marks.
**Nora:** One. **Like** poles **repel**. **Unlike** poles **attract**.
**Stan:** Two. Field lines go **north to south**, never crossing. Earth's magnetic **south** pole is up north.
**Amy:** Three. **Ammeter** in **series**, measuring **amps**. **Voltmeter** **across**, in **parallel**, measuring **volts**.
**Dimitri:** Four. More lamps in **series** means **dimmer**. Never brighter. Trust me.
**Sol:** Five. Switch off the current, and an electromagnet's magnetism **disappears**.
**Eddie:** Six! Current is **not** used up! Every Eddie comes back!
**Cecil:** Seven. Metals **conduct**. Plastic and rubber **insulate**. A rubber band is not a wire.
**Narrator:** Drawer 8B will return.
**Cecil:** Vic. Ten years in a drawer together. Anything you'd like to say?
**Cecil:** ...Turn the camera off.
